newsitem.title: UK: Venezuela comes under pressure in Brady market.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela comes under pressure in Brady market.

text.p: Venezuela Brady prices fell on Thursday, weighed by concerns of growing social unrest over government policies, traders said.
The rest of the market was also mostly under pressure, following Thursday's dip in New York.
Traders said they were worried protests against the Venezuelan government could lead to President Rafael Caldera's easing up on market reforms.
However, ANZ analyst Jerome Booth said the government was committed to reform and expected the International Monetary Fund to be sensitive to the social pressures Caldera faces.
"I'm a buyer at the lows," he said, though he added that more sparks could send debt prices lower yet.

A key issue will be whether the government raises gasoline prices, which in the past, has led to widespread unrest. The government said it has not yet decided on the issue, but the IMF is expected to seek another increase.
Other Latin American debt slipped, including Argentina despite reports it might get a credit rating upgrade.
Elsewhere, there was little movement, with Russia holding steady after the pricing of its two billion mark ($1.2 billion) Eurobond, set at 370 basis points over the German government bonds.
Traders were waiting to see the make-up of the new Russian government, but most assume it will be market-friendly, with more pro-reformists in the cabinet.
Several traders said Russian debt was underpriced after the latest general market correction.
Booth said he expected spreads to narrow sharply in the short-term, especially if the government gets tax reforms in place.
